newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Turkey disagree on Iraq, Israel.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Turkey disagree on Iraq, Israel.

text.p: Egypt and Turkey disagreed openly on northern Iraq and Turkish-Israeli military cooperation on Wednesday during a visit to Egypt by Turkey's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Abdullah Gul.
Gul met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and gave him Turkey's explanation for its military incursion against Iraqi Kurdish bases in northern Iraq, officials said.
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in pursuit of separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use the region to launch raids into Turkey.
He said it was a legitimate response to what he called "terrorism" by the PKK, which is fighting for an independent Kurdish state in southeastern Turkey.
But Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters later that there were other ways to deal with northern Iraq, where the Baghdad government has no control on the ground.
"We cannot agree to Iraqi territory becoming a free-for-all where you can go in and out as though there is no state, regardless of the current situation in Iraq," he said.
"It's true that Iraq has a special situation. There are U.N. forces and observers there and there are many other ways to deal with this situation," he added.
"The important thing now is to put an end to this business of going into Iraqi territory and the operations directed at the communities in the area," he said.

Gul said Turkey could not set a date for a Turkish withdrawal from northern Iraq. "What we can say is that the operation has achieved its aims and that as soon as possible the area will have been cleaned out and the Turkish forces will go back to their places," he added.

Moussa said: "He (Gul) listened with interest to what President Mubarak said on this subject -- that it is important to respect the integrity and unity of Iraqi territory and that what is happening in northern Iraq causes us grave concern."

On Turkish-Israeli defence cooperation, which has worried Egypt and other Arab states for months, the Egyptian minister said it was not for Egypt to ask Israel and Turkey to abandon their contacts or relations.

"But these relations must not damage the situation in the region or the process of restoring stability. The present situation in the peace process is very tense and this attitude makes things more tense. It is not propitious even from the point of view of timing," he added.
But Gul said Turkish-Israeli relations could not damage the interests of other countries in the region.
Gul gave Mubarak a message from Turkish President Suleyman Demirel, in answer to a message from Mubarak.
He said Demirel's message did not mention an economic summit of eight Islamic states in Istanbul next Sunday but this did come up in Gul's talks with Mubarak.
Egyptian foreign ministry sources said on Tuesday that Amr Moussa rather than President Mubarak would head the Egyptian delegation to the summit.
